candidates.attacker_control: The full text of the YAML/OpenAPI document that the application parses. Reachable when the caller passes user/integration-supplied content as a string (SwaggerParser.readWithInfo(String) line 99, SwaggerParser.parse(String) -> Swagger20Parser.convertToSwagger line 121), when a spec is fetched from an attacker-influenced file/URL (Swagger20Parser.readWithInfo line 64, Swagger20Parser.read -> convertToSwagger), and through external $ref documents resolved during SwaggerResolver.resolve() (ResolverCache.loadRef -> DeserializationUtils.deserializeIntoTree line 127 -> readYamlTree). A YAML payload with a !! tag and a leading character other than '{' takes the SnakeYAML branch instead of the Jackson JSON branch.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The JSON branch uses Jackson readTree and is unaffected; DeserializationUtils.deserialize(...) with a String uses swagger-core Yaml.mapper() (Jackson YAML) and is also not affected, so only the raw-SnakeYAML helpers are in scope. No test in the snapshot relies on unsafe YAML tags or on arbitrary type instantiation (AnchorTest only exercises anchors/aliases, which SafeConstructor also supports), so a safe-constructor remediation would not break existing behaviour. The exact SnakeYAML version is a transitive dependency not visible in this snapshot, so I could not confirm the resolved version from the repository alone; however, the unsafe behaviour of the no-arg Yaml() constructor is a property of SnakeYAML 1.x, which is the line used by swagger-core 1.5.x-era dependencies. I also considered whether the intended issue could instead be the ref-based SSRF/LFI or the opt-in TRUST_ALL TLS bypass; those are recorded as rejected leads.
candidates.impact: Parsing an untrusted spec is not a safe operation: an attacker can cause instantiation of attacker-chosen Java classes while the library parses YAML. Where a suitable gadget chain, JSR-223 scripting engine, or JNDI-capable class is on the classpath, this can escalate to remote code execution in the parsing application (server-side spec import/validation/CI use cases); without a gadget it still allows unexpected object construction/side effects and resource-exhaustion YAML constructs (e.g., alias expansion), i.e., integrity and availability impact across the trust boundary between the spec supplier and the parser host.
candidates.prerequisites: Application must parse attacker-influenced YAML through swagger-parser (common when accepting third-party or uploaded OpenAPI documents). SnakeYAML must be on the classpath: it is a transitive dependency (swagger-core 1.5.15 -> jackson-dataformat-yaml -> snakeyaml) and is used directly here, but its resolved version is not declared in this snapshot. Full code execution additionally requires a usable gadget/JSR-223 engine or JNDI-capable class on the application classpath; without one, the impact is arbitrary object instantiation and its side effects plus possible denial of service.
candidates.root_cause: DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree() and readYamlValue() construct org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml with its no-argument constructor, which uses SnakeYAML's permissive Constructor (not SafeConstructor). Loading a YAML document therefore honours explicit global tags such as !!com.example.Class, instantiating arbitrary Java types from data supplied by whoever provides the spec, instead of restricting the result to plain data types (maps, lists, scalars, dates). The result is then converted to a JsonNode and returned to the caller as a successfully parsed Swagger document.
candidates.title: Untrusted YAML specs parsed with SnakeYAML's unrestricted constructor (arbitrary Java type instantiation)
candidates.trace: 1) Public string API: SwaggerParser.readWithInfo(String) (SwaggerParser.java:89) checks the first character; YAML goes to DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree (SwaggerParser.java:99). 2) Location API: Swagger20Parser.readWithInfo(location, auths) (Swagger20Parser.java:37-58) obtains bytes from RemoteUrl/file/classpath and calls readYamlTree at line 64; the SwaggerParser.read() path reaches the same sink via convertToSwagger (Swagger20Parser.java:105, 121). 3) Resolver path: SwaggerResolver.resolve() -> PathsProcessor/ModelProcessor/... -> ResolverCache.loadRef (ResolverCache.java:112-127) reads an external file/URL and calls deserializeIntoTree, which calls readYamlTree (DeserializationUtils.java:13-21) when a definition path is present. 4) Sink: readYamlTree/readYamlValue build `new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml()` (DeserializationUtils.java:60 and 65) and call yaml.load(contents); with SnakeYAML 1.x the no-arg constructor selects the unrestricted Constructor, so `!!` global tags in the data select the Java class to instantiate before Json.mapper().convertValue is applied.
candidates.unverified: No build, test execution, or runtime reproduction was performed, and the resolved transitive SnakeYAML version is not present in the tree. Exploitability to code execution depends on application classpath gadgets, which cannot be established from this snapshot. The exact upstream remediation/commit was not consulted (no network/ground truth), so this remains a source-evidence lead rather than a confirmed vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data (unsafe SnakeYAML Constructor)

coverage_summary: Scope: 310 files at the repository root, 309 model-visible (1 path/name excluded as sensitive); two Maven modules (swagger-parser, swagger-compat-spec-parser) with 102 main Java files and 46 test Java files. P1 index: 148 Java files parsed, 13 files omitted, syntax-only relations (no control flow, no data flow, no semantic resolution); all candidate edges were checked against source text. I reviewed all main sources of the swagger-parser module (SwaggerParser, Swagger20Parser, SwaggerResolver, ResolverCache, all processors, RefUtils, RemoteUrl, ClasspathHelper, PathUtils, DeserializationUtils, HostAuthorizationValue/ManagedValue, SwaggerDeserializationResult) and the compat module's security-relevant code (SwaggerCompatConverter, SwaggerLegacyParser, readers/HttpClient/authentication, migrators, validators, MutableJsonTree, APIFileDownload, SwaggerJsonSchemaFactory), plus the key tests and fixtures that constrain ref/YAML behaviour (AnchorTest, RelativeReferenceTest, NetworkReferenceTests, LocalReferenceTests, ResolverCacheTest, RefUtilsTest, RemoteUrlTest, SwaggerParserTest/ReaderTest, issue-1261.yaml, nested-file-references fixtures). Not exhaustively reviewed: the full 63 KB SwaggerDeserializer.java body, the large sample JSON/YAML resources (e.g., public.json, marvel.json, petstore-codegen.yaml), and every test assertion. No build, tests, scanners, or payloads were executed.
limitations: No compilation or execution was performed; all findings are source-level and the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

Dependency versions (notably the transitive SnakeYAML version and its exact constructor semantics) are not vendored in the snapshot and could not be verified locally; exploitability to RCE depends on application classpath gadgets that are outside this tree.
The P1 relation index is syntactic only (no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution) and omits 13 files; those omitted files and the one sensitive-path-excluded file were not inspected.
The 63 KB SwaggerDeserializer.java and the very large sample resources were not read line-by-line, so a second independent issue could exist there that this review did not surface.
No ground-truth/advisory/commit information was consulted, so it is not established that the submitted lead matches any particular upstream fix or advisory.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF/arbitrary local file read through external $ref resolution: RemoteUrl.urlToString() opens any URL/scheme with no host or scheme restriction (RemoteUrl.java:93-133), and RefUtils.readExternalRef() resolves relative refs with parentDirectory.resolve(file).normalize() with no containment check (RefUtils.java:116-145), so a spec can make the parser fetch internal URLs or read files outside the spec directory (including absolute paths).
rejected_leads.reason: The code-level reach is real, but resolving remote and relative refs (including parent-directory refs such as ../common/... used in nested-file-references fixtures and RelativeReferenceTest/NetworkReferenceTests) is the library's documented core behaviour, so I could not attribute a distinct fixable root cause with security intent; impact overlaps the submitted candidate's trust-boundary argument. Left unsubmitted to respect the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: RemoteUrl creates an all-trusting TLS socket factory and hostname verifier when the system property <RemoteUrl class>.trustAll is true (RemoteUrl.java:28-87).
rejected_leads.reason: The bypass is opt-in via a JVM system property set by the deployer and is documented in the README as a knowingly dangerous workaround; it is not attacker-controlled by default, so it is a hardening/conﬁguration concern rather than a vulnerability in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: RemoteUrl.urlToString reads the whole response character-by-character with no timeouts or size limit (RemoteUrl.java:93-152), allowing slow/huge responses to tie up or exhaust the parsing process.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible DoS hardening gap but diffuse, dependency/config dependent, and weaker source evidence than the submitted candidate; not submitted separately.

rejected_leads.lead: ClasspathHelper.loadFileFromClasspath falls back to classpath resource loading for any not-found location (ClasspathHelper.java:11-32), which callers can influence (Swagger20Parser, RefUtils).
rejected_leads.reason: The same callers already read arbitrary filesystem paths by design, so the incremental disclosure is limited and no clear fix boundary is visible; left unconfirmed.

summary: Defensive review of the swagger-parser 1.x snapshot (modules/swagger-parser and modules/swagger-compat-spec-parser). I traced the parsing entry points, the ref-resolution machinery, remote URL handling, and JSON/YAML deserialization. Strongest source-evidenced issue: untrusted YAML is loaded with SnakeYAML's permissive no-argument constructor (DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree/readYamlValue), which permits arbitrary Java type instantiation from YAML global tags and is reachable from the public parse APIs (SwaggerParser.readWithInfo(String), SwaggerParser.parse(String), Swagger20Parser.read/readWithInfo for remote or local YAML specs, and external $ref documents via ResolverCache.loadRef -> deserializeIntoTree). No runtime verification was performed; dependency versions are not vendored in the snapshot. Other plausible leads (SSRF/LFI through external refs, opt-in TRUST_ALL TLS bypass, no response size/time limits in RemoteUrl) are described as rejected/unconfirmed rather than submitted.
